## Summary

WP-036 slice 2. An Owner or Admin can now open a Church Document and edit it on a paper page. The toolbar uses Tiptap's free parts, restyled with Everyfield's fonts, colors and spacing in light and dark mode. They can type, set text styles and headings, use bold, italic, underline, links and tags, add lists, quotes, dividers, spacers and page breaks, move and delete blocks, save with a status, and wipe the document with "Delete all content". Undo and Redo work for each action. Preview shows the real PDF of the saved revision. A Member still sees only the PDF and the downloads.

This round also does the five things Sebastian asked for after his try-out on Nov 1. The first card in "New from template" shows its full border. The template list has a search box and pages, so 50 or more templates stay easy to browse. The dialog keeps one height, so its top edge stays put while you type a search, even with no results. Bold, italic and the serif headings now print in the PDF. Leaving the editor with unsaved changes asks in an Everyfield dialog, not a browser popup.

## What changed and why

- **Free parts only** (Sebastian, Nov 1, 1:11 AM ET: "I don't want to pay, use whatever is free"). The editor uses the MIT `@tiptap/*` packages and copies of Tiptap's free UI components. No Tiptap Pro package, plan, registry or paid component (no slash menu, no selection toolbar). A test fails on any non-MIT `@tiptap/*` dependency, any `@tiptap-pro/*` package and any Tiptap line in an `.npmrc`.
- **The schema is the format.** The editor's extensions use the node and mark names and attributes of `everyfield.doc/1`, so `getJSON()` is the document body. An attribute the file leaves out stays out of the JSON. The only normalization on the way out is that ProseMirror writes no empty `attrs` and no empty `content: []`; the format reads both the same as a missing key (`document-json.ts`).
- **Paper page** at the document's paper width and margins, in the PDF's fonts and sizes, with heading numbers as the PDF prints them (01, 02, 1.1). Page breaks show as a labelled gap between sheets. Later-slice blocks (columns, box, image, write-in, slot, table, inline field) show read-only with their kind as a label and are selected whole. The "Template, not legal advice" notice and its Locked badge sit outside the editable body.
- **Toolbar** from Tiptap's free primitives, mark buttons, Undo/Redo buttons and link popover, restyled with `packages/ui` tokens (`editor/tiptap/styles.ts`). The bulleted list, numbered list and quote buttons are Tiptap's free ready-made `list-button` and `blockquote-button` (the node name is `quote`; one Undo reverses one click). The combined text-style menu (paragraph styles and headings in one menu), the tag, the block insert menu and the move and delete controls use the same primitives, because Tiptap has no free ready-made part for them (see the README of the copied folder). The link popover refuses any address that does not start with `https://`, `http://` or `mailto:` and says so.
- **Block actions** (Insert, Move up, Move down, Delete, Delete all content) are one transaction each, so one Undo reverses one action. Keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Up, Down and Backspace.
- **Save** is a server action (`saveChurchDocument`) over the existing `documents.saveNative` path (one statement, expected revision, audit row). The editor keeps content, cursor and undo history after a save, and the header revision and download links move without `router.refresh`. Cmd/Ctrl+S saves. A conflict shows "Not saved" with the reason and Retry; the edits stay.
- **Preview** saves first when there are changes, then shows the PDF of the new revision through the same file route Download uses.
- **Members** get the same page as before. The stored document is not sent to their browser, and the editor chunk is a dynamic import rendered only for an Owner or Admin.
- **Unused Tiptap parts removed** (`6b97c92`). The copied `dropdown-menu.tsx` keeps only the parts the toolbar uses (no sub, group or radio menus), and `button.tsx`, `link-popover.tsx` and `use-composed-ref.ts` lose their unused default exports. The README of the copied folder records it. No behavior change; no caller used them.
- **Document-template path changed.** `packages/domain/src/documents/layouts/blocks.tsx`, `layouts/doc.tsx` and `doc-docx.ts` now import `LEGAL_NOTICE` from `@everyfield/contracts/documents` (no re-export). Round 3 also changes `packages/domain/src/documents/fonts.ts` (owner item 3). All four paths are in `mergePolicy.documentTemplates`, so this PR waits for Sebastian: `evf ship` stops after the verifier and `evf approve` merges.

### Sebastian's five items from the Nov 1 try-out

From the coordinator notes of 1:06 PM, 1:14 PM and 3:37 PM ET.

1. **The first template card's border.** The scroll area of "New from template" cut off the top edge of the first card's ring. The list now has 4 px of top padding inside the scroll area, so the ring and the focus outline show in full.
2. **Search and pages in "New from template".** A search box matches every typed word against the template name, description and category. The list shows ten templates for each page, with "Showing 11–20 of 60" and a pager. A search with no result says so. The search box clears with the browser's own clear button or by deleting the text; the separate "Clear search" button is gone (`0dec90f`). Screen readers hear the count of matching templates. A fixture of 60 templates at `/design/documents/templates` proves it without database rows.
3. **Bold in the PDF.** The cause was the font loader, not the editor. It loaded each face with `new URL(`./fonts/${file}`)`. The bundler could not name the files from that template URL, so it shipped one file and every face embedded DM Sans Regular. The loader now has one literal `new URL` for each face, and Bold, Italic, Bold Italic, the figures and DM Serif Display each embed their own font program. File: `packages/domain/src/documents/fonts.ts`.
4. **In-app leave dialog.** A link, the app navigation or the Back button with unsaved changes opens an Everyfield dialog (the `packages/ui` `Dialog`, light and dark): "Leave without saving?" with Cancel, Leave without saving and Save and leave. Save and leave saves first and then follows the link. A failed save keeps the page and shows "Not saved" with Retry. The editor has no `window.confirm`, `alert` or `prompt`. Closing or reloading the tab still shows only the browser's own `beforeunload` prompt, because browsers do not let a page replace it.
5. **The picker keeps its top edge and height while searching** (3:37 PM: "the top of the modal doesn't shift ... ideally the height also doesn't vary, even if results are 0"). The dialog was centered and sized to its content, so each search result count moved its top edge: at 1440 px the top sat at 12, 303 and 324 px for the full list, one result and no result. The dialog now has one fixed height, `min(800px, 100dvh - 24px)`, on its `DialogContent` (`ChurchLibrary.tsx`, `5269d71`). The top stays at 22 px at 390 and at 50 px at 1440, and the height stays 800 px, for the full list, one result and no result, in light and dark. The list scrolls inside; a short result leaves white space below it.

### Rulings and shared changes

- The page stays white paper in dark mode, as the PDF is. Only the editor chrome follows the theme. Reversible (CSS variables in `editor.css`).
- Header and footer live on the document node as attributes, so Undo and Redo of "Delete all content" bring body, header and footer back together. ProseMirror cannot redraw a page that loses every block in the same update as a document-node attribute, so `EmptyDocumentRedraw` clears the stale blocks (caught by the browser test).
- "Delete all content" removes the header and footer regions; it does not keep empty regions.
- Heading numbers follow the renderer exactly: level 2 counts every level-2 heading and prints two digits, level 3 prints "h2.h3".
- Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down/Backspace move and delete blocks. Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down and Option+Shift+Arrow already extend text selections in browsers.
- Shared files touched: `apps/web/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` (Tiptap, `@floating-ui/react` and `radix-ui` pinned exactly), `apps/web/eslint.config.mjs` (the three React-compiler rules `set-state-in-effect`, `refs`, `immutability` are off for the copied `editor/tiptap/` folder only), and the `test:unit` script (one new test file).

Fixes for the round 1 findings:

1. **Toolbar on load.** The copied hooks set visibility in an effect and read a hydration snapshot whose editor is `null`, so Bold, Italic, Underline, Link and the list buttons stayed hidden until the first transaction. The hooks now derive visibility on each render, `useTiptapEditor` returns the editor itself, and the toolbar draws again when the view mounts. The browser test fails on the old code (it timed out waiting for Bold) and passes now. 19 buttons show on load; the rest screenshots show them.
2. **Ready-made list and quote buttons.** Copied `list-button` and `blockquote-button` with their hooks (README and the table above name them). The toggles stay one chain, so one Undo reverses one click. The PR body and the README no longer say Tiptap has no ready-made part for them. The text-style menu (styles and headings in one) has no ready-made match.
3. **Back button.** An unsaved document pushes one sentinel history entry, so the first Back press stays on the page and asks first. Since round 3 the question is the Everyfield leave dialog (see the owner items above), not a browser confirm. The sentinel stays after a save, so one extra Back press is needed then (one entry, not one per save).
4. **Hand check.** See the note above the table.
5. **Other findings.** The PR title now names the slice. The `spacer.tsx` row is gone. The notice text is one `LEGAL_NOTICE` constant in `@everyfield/contracts/documents`, imported directly by the PDF layout, the Word file and the editor. `refusedWith` has a narrow return type and the server action drops its branch. The refusal messages moved to `refusal.ts` so the integration test reads the Member message the save action shows. The browser test asserts Move down is disabled on the last block. Timing now runs through `bin/evf timing`.

Screenshots (Chromium, 390 and 1440 px, light and dark, on head `104ec3ac`): toolbar at rest `shots/<width>-<theme>-rest.png` in the [evidence index](https://everyfield-evidence.t3.storage.dev/evf-evidence/WP-036/5c452801a6f8f046cf4832af63fbc722/index.html). The other state screenshots (open text-style menu, link popover with its message, active bold and tag, Locked notice with its tooltip) are unchanged since the round 1 head `d3b8fdd`: [round 1 evidence](https://everyfield-evidence.t3.storage.dev/evf-evidence/WP-036/ea119a5c2c3e6d9edc6b83a13cbfd776/index.html). No "before" screenshots: the page had no editor before.

### Load and speed (criterion 15)

`bin/evf timing` on a production preview of the exact head and a quiet local database, 20 samples, no non-qualifying samples ([report](https://everyfield-evidence.t3.storage.dev/evf-evidence/WP-036/5c452801a6f8f046cf4832af63fbc722/timing-production.json)): from navigation to the typed character in the editor, **148 to 215 ms** against the 1000 ms budget. The probe saw round trips of 2 ms at the 50th percentile and 11 ms at most. Round 1 measured 926 to 942 ms with a private script on the shared development database: that number was limited by the round trip to the remote database (about 400 ms of page stream) plus the editor chunk. The quiet local database has no such trip, so the new number shows the app's own cost, not production latency. The set clicks the first body paragraph before it types.

- Save of the forked policy, from the click to "Saved": 211 to 230 ms in round 1 (shared database). Not re-measured; the save path did not change.
- The statement count of the document page is unchanged by construction (the same one `readChurch` call; the stored document is only passed on for an Owner or Admin). The documents integration suite (69 tests) passes except three files that need the CI database guard; the changed file passes.

## Risks and accepted exceptions

- Merge route: the PR changes document-template paths, including `packages/domain/src/documents/fonts.ts` (see above), so it needs Sebastian's approval through `evf approve`.
- Door: two-way. A revert removes the editor, and Church Documents go back to read-only.
- Blast radius: the Church Document page for an Owner or Admin, the "New from template" dialog, and the fonts of every exported PDF (see the font fix below). Members and the library load none of the editor code. New dependencies add about 150 KB to the editor chunk only.
- Leave guard: a `popstate` sentinel entry and the in-app leave dialog. After a save the entry stays, so the next Back press goes to the same page once before it leaves. The browser test checks the dialog for a link and for Back in Chromium only; I did not check it in WebKit.
- Tab close and reload: they show only the browser's own `beforeunload` prompt. Browsers do not let a page replace it.
- Font fix: it changes every exported PDF, not only edited ones. Bold, italic and serif text in all templates now print in their real faces, as the theme intended. Earlier exports printed those as DM Sans Regular.
- WebKit: I checked the editor in Chromium only. Screenshots and the editor browser tests are Chromium. The template picker test runs in Chromium and WebKit.
- The save server action is not one of the HTTP requests in `tests/integration/writes/requests.mjs`; its write is the existing one-statement `documents.saveNative` (budget 1) and the CI statement check covers that.
- "Hand check": see the note above the table. Undo and Redo columns are the test's exact JSON comparison, not a look at each picture.
- Hydration: `useTiptapEditor` now returns the editor on the server render too. The toolbar renders the same on the server and the client (the view is not mounted on the server, so the mark buttons are hidden there and show after mount). The browser test collects page errors and none appeared.
- The picker dialog is always 800 px tall, or the window height less 24 px on a short window. A search with few results leaves white space below the list; Sebastian asked for a fixed height over a dialog that shrinks.
- The 60-template list is a design fixture. The real library has fewer templates today, so the pager shows only when a church has more than ten.
- Copied Tiptap files keep Tiptap's code and need three React-compiler lint rules off (folder only), listed above.
- The Locked badge tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus (Radix tooltip). I did not test a touch screen.
